unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.2 - THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design a ''Virtual Museum about Life in the Universe and Future'' focussing on space travel technologies, the concept of space tourism, and science fiction imagination. Students will start with researching different aspects of rockets, satellites, lunar missions, and interplanetary travel. They will use Web 2.0 tools or AI technologies and they will design each section with pictures, descriptions, timelines or short videos. The museum should include creative elements like charts, interactive timelines, and detailed illustrations of spacecraft and futuristic cities. Additionally, they may add science fiction stories and metaphorical visuals to represent futuristic ideas. They will present their virtual museum to the class by explaining the key elements and how each part reflects the future possibilities of space exploration, technological advancements, and interplanetary life. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as lifestyles and culture on leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city; urban trends and technology; performing arts (dance, theatre) and visual arts (painting, sculpture, architecture) in the city'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the after prep year 10 of an upper secondary school may know what lifestyles and culture on leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city; urban trends and technology; performing arts (dance, theatre) and visual arts (painting, sculpture, architecture) in the city mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 10 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 10 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as lifestyles and culture on leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city; urban trends and technology; performing arts (dance, theatre) and visual arts (painting, sculpture, architecture) in the city'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as preparatory practices. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about lifestyles, culture, and leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Descriptive Writing Students work in groups to describe urban life and events by using the target grammar. Each group chooses a topic such as a recent urban art festival or a cultural exhibition in the city. They collaborate to write a descriptive paragraph. They create visuals and prepare a short presentation. An example paragraph for the presentation can be as follows: ''Last weekend, an art festival was held in the main square of the city. Beautiful murals were painted by talented artists, and live music performances were organised to attract visitors. Sculptures were exhibited in the central gallery and some awards were given to the best work of art. The event was attended by many residents and it helped to promote cultural appreciation''. Each group will present their work by using images or drawings to enrich their presentation and engage the audience. After the presentation, the teacher gives feedback on the use of the language including accuracy, use of target vocabulary, target grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe lifestyles, culture, and leisure activities in the neighbourhood and city in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Matching Vocabulary with Definitions The teacher prepares a worksheet related to life in the neighbourhood, city, and social life to help students practice target vocabulary and grammar. The worksheet includes two activities: first, students match the target words such as resident, coexistence, and sculpture with simple definitions or visuals (e.g. ''A person who lives in a neighbourhood → Resident'' or ''A public sale of goods to the highest bidder → Auction''). Second, students complete sentences using the correct forms of the ''Passive Voice in past tenses such as ''A local festival _______ (organise) in the city centre last weekend'' (was organised) or ''Sculptures _______ (display) at the city’s art gallery last month'' (were being displayed). This worksheet is designed to improve vocabulary learning and to practise the use of the ''Passive Voice''. The teacher gives feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, target grammar and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
